Subject: Quick sync — renewal metrics after quant pilot

Marissa,

Thanks again for running the quantization pilot with our inference stack last month. The team and I reviewed the output and have a couple of follow-ups before the renewal next quarter:

- Token spend fell ~18% month-over-month after we flipped to int8 for the encoder, but tail-latency increased on long-context (>4k) calls.
- Our SRE flagged occasional KV cache miss storms during heavy batch windows — we see spikes in cold-starts.
- We expect a 30–50% expansion in embeddings workload for a feature launch in Q4 and want to understand runway options for capacity while keeping unit cost in check.

Can you share a short recap of usage trends, a performance ROI recap (tokens, latency, cost), and any recommended commitment path that would let us cover the Q4 uplift without overcommitting? Appreciate the transparent numbers — the procurement team will want a concrete mutual action plan.

—Clara
Principal Product Manager
HelixAI

Clara — thanks for the clear summary. High level recap below and attaching a short packet with the underlying logs. I also looped in Soojin (solutions) since there are a couple of ops knobs that matter for the cache behavior.

Executive summary:
- Token economics: your month-over-month token spend dropped 18% after int8 encoder quant. Gross token count decreased ~16% and average per-token compute charge decreased due to shorter tail execution on the encoder. Net cost savings estimate: ~15% for generation-heavy flows. (See helix_q2_quant_perf_report.pdf)
- Latency: median latency improved ~8% for short-context requests; p95 increased ~12% on requests >4k tokens. This matches expected attention compute variance with low-precision kernels at extreme sequence lengths.
- KV cache: cache hit rate dipped during spikes; we see a correlation with batched cold-starts when ephemeral instances spin up. Suggested mitigations: sticky instances for hot prefixes + a small warm pool.
- Q4 uplift projection: your forecast (+40% embeddings volume in October) would push peak RPS into a new tranche. Two pragmatic routes: 1) a 3-month capacity bridge (reserved burst lanes + true-up) to cover the launch window, or 2) a longer 12-month committed plan with staged tranches and a quantization performance SLA carveout.

Attached: helix_q2_quant_perf_report.pdf (3 pages), kv_cache_hitrate_Q2.csv.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal alignment call (30m) to confirm the Q4 volume curve and acceptable unit economics.
2) I'll send a 1-page bridge proposal (3-month reserved + true-up) for procurement.
3) Soojin to provide ops checklist for cache warm pools and prefetch settings.

Are you available Wed 8/5 10–11am PT? If so, I can draft the bridge and include a pricing sketch.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Clara Gong <clara.gong@helixai.com>, Ethan Price <ethan.price@helixai.com>
Subject: Re: Quick sync — renewal metrics after quant pilot

Marissa / Karthik — adding ops detail and a quick runbook for the cache pattern we observed. Short version below; full checklist attached.

- Root cause: miss storms occur when a batch of new prefixes enters the system simultaneously (UX rollout) and autoscaler spins up ephemeral workers that start with empty KV caches.
- Mitigation (fast): maintain a 2–3 instance warm pool pinned to the embeddings model for 48–72 hours around expected launches. This reduces cold-start miss rate by ~65% in our tests.
- Mitigation (medium): enable prefetch for top-100 prefixes with an adaptive TTL; this reduces sustained miss rate and keeps memory safe.
- SLA note: quantized kernels can have variable p95 at >4k; we can add an SLA carveout for long-context requests and provide a fallback route to float a higher-precision model when p95 spikes. That avoids regression to your UX.

I'll attach the ops checklist and a short config snippet for the warm pool sizing. If procurement prefers not to add long-term reserved capacity, the 3-month bridge with warm-pool ops is cost-efficient.

Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer — Performance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Renewal runway proposal — 3-month bridge + true-up (sketch)

Clara — thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion, attached is a concise mutual action plan and the bridge sketch. Key points: 

- Bridge offer: 3 months of reserved burst capacity sized for 1.4x your current peak embeddings tranche (covers the projected +40% uplift) starting 2026-10-01.
- Pricing: blended unit price sits ~7% below on-demand for the bridge; if final volume ends up >1.4x we apply a 30-day true-up at a negotiated step rate.
- Ops commitments: Redwood will maintain a 3-instance warm pool for the embeddings model during the 3-month window, enable prefetch for top prefixes, and monitor KV cache hit-rate daily. We'll provide a daily health digest during the first two weeks post-launch.
- Quality guardrails: fallback routing to a higher-precision model for requests >4k tokens if p95 crosses the agreed threshold (1500ms) more than 3x in a 24h period. Fallback is free during the bridge term.

Requested next actions from HelixAI:
1) Procurement: confirm acceptance of the bridge pricing sketch or propose counter (we can provide a redline doc).
2) Engineering: share the expected hourly RPS profile for Oct 2026 by 8/14 so we can finalize pool sizing.
3) Legal: indicate whether a 30-day true-up clause is acceptable.

I'll attach the proposed_capacity_bridge_v3.docx and a 1-page ROI recap from the pilot. If you confirm procurement interest, I can circulate a formal SOW.

Appreciate the partnership — happy to jump on a call to walk through specifics this week.

—Marissa
Account Exec — Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference
